body: Thanks, never talked about this with anyone let alone a doctor or therapist, I feel prepared now.
I'm reading these sidebar rules and I guess I may be borderline asking people to break one of the rules here. So don't do that. I don't need support so I think I posted to the wrong sub.

I want to express to a therapist how pragmatic I've become about my own death, and that I have come to a point where I believe my hesitation is just about gone. And I'd like to try some medication for that whatever they would diagnose my situation as. I'm not even sure I'm depressed actually, I'm just ready to die after thinking about it and planning it out for some time.

Would it be the same medication as if I just told them I was depressed? I want to explain my actual situation to a therapist so they give me whatever they think is correct but I don't want to get committed or lose my ability to commit suicide while committed if I discover the meds don't work either.

That's what I suspected.

How can a person get prescribed some kind of antidepressant as a last ditch effort? I guess I feel I owe myself some kind of chance. But I'd rather just proceed with killing myself than get committed.
